questions.prompt: What is the mean of the following flight prices? $388, 397, 397, 427, 432, 782, 872
hints: Sum all prices, then divide by 7.
The mean is not the middle value.

questions.prompt: The middle value of an ordered data set is called the ___.
hints: It's the value that splits the data into two equal parts.
Starts with 'm'.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The median is the middle value when the data are ordered.

hints: Order the data first.
With 7 numbers, the 4th value is the median.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The mode is the only measure suitable for qualitative (categorical) data.
hints: Only one measure deals with frequency of categories.
You cannot add or sort labels meaningfully.
questions.prompt: Which measure of central tendency can be used for qualitative data?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: A data set with two modes is called bimodal.
questions.prompt: A data set has two values that both appear most frequently. What term describes this data set?
hints: It has two modes.
The prefix 'bi-' means two.

questions.prompt: A student's test mean is 86, midterm 96, final 82, lab 98, homework 100. The weights are: 0.50, 0.15, 0.20, 0.10, 0.05. What is the weighted mean?
hints: Multiply each score by its weight and sum.
Weights sum to 1.

questions.prompt: To approximate the mean of a grouped frequency distribution, use the class ___ as representative values.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Class midpoints are used to approximate the mean of grouped data.
hints: It's the average of lower and upper class limits.
Not class boundaries.

questions.prompt: For a grouped frequency distribution, if sum of (midpoint × frequency) = 2089 and n = 50, what is the approximate mean?
hints: Divide the total (2089) by 50.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: In a symmetric, unimodal distribution, the mean, median, and mode are approximately equal.
hints: In symmetry, the two halves are mirror images.
All three measures coincide.
questions.prompt: A histogram is symmetric and unimodal. Which statement is true?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: A tail on the left indicates left‑skewed (negatively skewed).
questions.prompt: A distribution with a tail extending to the left is called ___ skewed.
hints: The tail points in that direction.
Also called negatively skewed.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: In right‑skewed data, mean > median > mode (usually).
questions.prompt: In a right‑skewed distribution, which measure is usually largest: mean, median, or mode?
hints: The mean is pulled toward the tail.
Think of income data with very high earners.

questions.prompt: An extreme value that is much higher or lower than the rest of the data is called an:
hints: It lies 'outside' the main cluster.
Starts with 'o'.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: An extreme value far from the rest is an outlier.
The mean is sensitive to outliers.
hints: It uses every data value in its calculation.
It gets pulled in the direction of the extreme.
questions.prompt: The ___ is most affected by outliers.

hints: It is resistant to extreme values.
It stays near the center of the bulk of data.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The median is preferred when outliers are present.
questions.prompt: If a data set has an outlier, which measure of central tendency is generally preferred: mean or median?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: A uniform distribution has all bars at approximately the same height.
questions.prompt: Which of the following shapes describes a distribution where all bars are roughly the same height?
hints: It's also called rectangular.
All classes have similar frequencies.
